65064-the-old-ones.title: The Old Ones
65064-the-old-ones.creator: Unknown
65064-the-old-ones.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. te end of the office, the first five now ticketed "closed" and the "closed" sign lying on top of the sixth, the 100-year case. He gazed on down the row--110, 120, 130, 140 and the rest--and sighed deeply. Futility washed over him, and an echo of the old story of the man who wrote his autobiography taking a year to write the doings of each day.

arxiv-2009-09795.title: Biases in Data Science Lifecycle
arxiv-2009-09795.creator: Dinh-an Ho dinh-an.ho@rwth-aachen.de, Oya Beyan beyan@fit.fraunhofer.de
arxiv-2009-09795.description: Abstract In recent years, data science has become an indispensable part of our society. Over time, we have become reliant on this technology because of its opportunity to gain value and new insights from data in any field - business, socializing, research and society.

arxiv-2012-06839.title: Loop effective model for Schwarzschild black hole: a modified μ ¯ \bar{\mu} dynamics
arxiv-2012-06839.creator: Mehdi Assanioussi, Lisa Mickel
arxiv-2012-06839.description: Abstract In this article, we introduce a new effective model for the Kantowski-Sachs spacetime in the context of loop quantum gravity, and we use it to evaluate departures from general relativity in the case of Schwarzschild black hole interior. The model is based on an effective Hamiltonian constructed via the regularized Thiemann identities in the μ ¯ \bar{\mu} -scheme.

arxiv-2012-14883.title: A hyperbolic proof of Pascal’s Theorem Thanks: Both authors were partially supported by FNR grant AGoLoM OPEN/16/11405402
arxiv-2012-14883.creator: Miguel Acosta, Jean-Marc Schlenker
arxiv-2012-14883.description:
A 2020 arXiv research paper by Miguel Acosta, Jean-Marc Schlenker. We provide a simple proof of Pascal’s Theorem on cyclic hexagons, as well as a generalization by Möbius, using hyperbolic geometry. Pascal’s Theorem

Blaise Pascal (1623–1662) is a towering intellectual figure of the XVII
th
century. He is credited with inventing and building the first mechanical calculator, the
Pascaline
, and with laying the foundations of probability theory, in particular in his correspondence with Fermat – he came up for instance with Pascal’s triangle.

arxiv-2207-12562.title: Fluctuation of Chern Numbers in a Parametric Random Matrix Model
arxiv-2207-12562.creator: Hung-Hwa Lin, Wei-Ting Kuo, Daniel P. Arovas, Yi-Zhuang You
arxiv-2207-12562.description: Abstract Band-touching Weyl points in Weyl semimetals give rise to many novel characteristics, one of which the presence of surface Fermi-arc states that is topologically protected. The number of such states can be computed by the Chern numbers at different momentum slices, which fluctuates with changing momentum and depends on the distribution of Weyl points in the Brillouin zone.

arxiv-2405-01265.title: Derivation of Dirac Exchange Interaction Potential from Quantum Plasma Kinetic Theory
arxiv-2405-01265.creator: Fernando Haas
arxiv-2405-01265.description: Abstract The Dirac exchange interaction is derived from recent quantum kinetic theory for collisionless plasmas. For this purpose, the kinetic equation is written in the semiclassical and long wavelength approximations. The validity of the model for real systems is worked out, in terms of temperature and density parameters.

arxiv-2501-04744.title: Exact computation of the color function for triangular element interfaces
arxiv-2501-04744.creator: Stéphane Zaleski
arxiv-2501-04744.description: Abstract The calculation of the volume enclosed by curved surfaces discretized into triangular elements, and a cube is of great importance in different domains, such as computer graphics and multiphase flow simulations. We propose a robust algorithm, the Front2VOF (F2V) algorithm, to address this problem. The F2V algorithm consists of two main steps.

arxiv-2507-15793.title: Regularized Low-Rank Adaptation for Few-Shot Organ Segmentation
arxiv-2507-15793.creator: Ghassen Baklouti ,🖂, Julio Silva-Rodríguez, Jose Dolz, Houda Bahig, Ismail Ben Ayed
arxiv-2507-15793.description: Abstract Parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) of pre-trained foundation models is increasingly attracting interest in medical imaging due to its effectiveness and computational efficiency. Among these methods, Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) is a notable approach based on the assumption that the adaptation inherently occurs in a low-dimensional subspace.

arxiv-2508-10656.title: Quantum-Guided Cluster Algorithms for Combinatorial Optimization
arxiv-2508-10656.creator: Peter J. Eder TUM, Garching, Germany Siemens AG, Germany peter-josef.eder@tum.de Aron Kerschbaumer Institute of Science and Technology Austria (ISTA) aron.kerschbaumer@ist.ac.at Jernej Rudi Finžgar TUM Garching, Germany BMW AG, Germany jernej-rudi.finzgar@tum.de Raimel A. Medina Institute of Science
arxiv-2508-10656.description: Abstract Finding the ground state of Ising spin glasses is notoriously difficult due to disorder and frustration. Often, this challenge is framed as a combinatorial optimization problem, for which a common strategy employs simulated annealing, a Monte Carlo (MC)-based algorithm that updates spins one at a time.

arxiv-2602-15694.title: Charm and strange meson fragmentation functions
arxiv-2602-15694.creator: Roberto C. da Silveira, Ian C. Cloët, Bruno El-Bennich, Fernando E. Serna
arxiv-2602-15694.description: Abstract Quark fragmentation functions describe the hadronization process of a quark where any of the final-state hadrons carries a fraction of its initial momentum. We compute these fragmentation functions for a cascade that includes pions, kaons, and the charmed D D and D s D_{s} mesons, starting from the elementary quark-to-meson fragmentation process.

arxiv-2602-19687.title: Exo Skryer: A JAX-accelerated sub-stellar atmospheric retrieval framework.
arxiv-2602-19687.creator: Elspeth K.H. Lee
arxiv-2602-19687.description: Abstract Contemporary exoplanet and brown dwarf atmospheric research relies heavily on retrieval frameworks to recover thermal and chemical properties and perform model comparison in an observational data-driven approach. However, the computational effort required for retrieval modelling has rapidly increased, driven by JWST data that covers large spectral intervals at moderate spectral resolutions, and ground-based, high-resolution spectroscopy.

pmc-12470727.title: Treatment Outcomes of Upside–Down Descemet Membrane Endothelial Keratoplasty
pmc-12470727.creator: Karolina Bonińska, Sławomir Cisiecki, Tomasz Dybek, Agnieszka Kardaszewska, Maciej Bednarski
pmc-12470727.description: Background: To present the management of upside–down Descemet membrane endothelial keratoplasty (DMEK) with intraoperative optical coherence tomography (iOCT). Methods: We report the case of a 74-year-old woman who underwent DMEK for Fuchs’ endothelial corneal dystrophy (FECD) of the right eye. Preoperative corrected distance visual acuity (CDVA) was 20/1500 (counting fingers [CF]), and the central corneal thickness (CCT) was 637 μm.

pmc-12582853.title: A Case of Breast Cancer with Cystic Axillary Lymph Node Metastasis
pmc-12582853.creator: Mariko Yoshino, Yoshiya Horimoto, Mutsumi Hayashi, Yuko Ueki, Yumiko Ishizuka, Hiroko Onagi, Takuo Hayashi, Kotaro Iijima, Goro Kutomi
pmc-12582853.description: INTRODUCTIONEncapsulated papillary carcinoma (EPC) is a relatively rare form of breast cancer and is often low grade. Even in cases of EPC with invasion, it rarely metastasizes. We herein report a case of EPC with invasion that presented with a cystic axillary lymph node metastasis that was highly characteristic on imaging.

pmc-12590340.title: The effects of a dietitian‐supported multidisciplinary nutrition intervention on optimizing nutrition care in older patients with hip fracture and at nutrition risk—A quality improvement study
pmc-12590340.creator: Tina Munk, Anne Marie Beck, Cecilie M Møller, Frederikke E Pudselykke, Guro ØH Mikkelsen, Heidrun T Filtenborg, Trine S Pedersen, Jens Peter Alva‐Jørgensen, Anne W Knudsen
pmc-12590340.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). IntroductionA 1‐day cross‐sectional study at our hospital found that only 22% of patients with hip fractures at nutrition risk met their energy and protein requirements during hospitalization. This study aimed to test whether closer collaboration between a clinical dietitian and ward staff, guided by the Model for Improvement, could optimize nutrition care for hospitalized older patients with hip fractures at nutrition risk.MethodA dietitian was embedded to facilitate staff‐led enhancements in nutrition care at an orthopedic ward in from September to December 2024.

pmc-13097505.creator: Russell B. O. Ouma, Silas M. Ngari, Joshua K. Kibet
pmc-13097505.description: Background and AimsThe therapeutic limitations of conventional cancer treatment currently deployed are driving the development and creation of new nano‐drugs. Prostate cancer (PCa) is a prevalent clinical problem in older men with a significant global incidence, with 1.5 million cases reported in 2022.

pmc-13519319.title: How I Teach Mechanical Ventilator Waveform Analysis: A Focus on Normal Ventilator Waveforms
pmc-13519319.creator: Michael Keller, Nitin Seam, Burton Lee
pmc-13519319.description: Identification and management of patient-ventilator asynchronies is a fundamental skill for the management of mechanical ventilation and often requires interpretation of mechanical ventilation waveform scalars. However, teaching mechanical ventilation waveform analysis can be challenging for educators due to the complexity of the material.

pmc-13545273.title: The Evolution of Medications for Obesity Management
pmc-13545273.creator: Jaskirath Gill, Priya Sumithran
pmc-13545273.description: This narrative review provides an overview of progress in the development of obesity medications, including a synthesis of data describing the efficacy and safety of currently available agents and emerging therapeutic options. Historically, many obesity medications have been withdrawn from the market due to safety concerns.

uslaw-usc-t38-s2403.title: 38 U.S.C. § 2403 — Memorial areas
uslaw-usc-t38-s2403.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t38-s2403.description: United States Code, Title 38 (Veterans’ Benefits); Part II (General Benefits); Chapter 24 (National Cemeteries And Memorials). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) The Secretary shall set aside, when available, suitable areas in national cemeteries to honor the memory of members of the Armed Forces and veterans— (1) who are missing in action; (2) whose remains have not been recovered or identified.
